title: eDNA African freshwater metagenomics pipeline: shotgun eDNA metagenomics workflow for African freshwater systems
description:
A modular Bash/SLURM workflow for Illumina paired-end environmental DNA (eDNA) shotgun metagenomes from African freshwater systems. It runs quality control (FastQC, MultiQC), deduplication (Clumpify), trimming (fastp), read-level taxonomic screening (Kraken2), per-sample assembly (MEGAHIT) and assembly assessment (QUAST), read mapping and coverage (BBMap, CoverM), domain separation of contigs (Tiara), prokaryotic genome binning and refinement (MetaBAT2, MaxBin2, DAS Tool) with quality and taxonomy (CheckM, GTDB-Tk, CAT/BAT), a eukaryotic branch with CAT classification of eukaryotic and mitochondrial contigs, reMAG binning and BUSCO quality, and paired cross-treatment summaries. It was first developed to test how library fragmentation affects eDNA signals across molecular, genomic, taxonomic and community scales, and can be adapted to rivers, lakes and caves.

Developed at KU Leuven in African freshwater eDNA research with the Royal Museum for Central Africa.
